name: Hanging Obelisk of Ramesses II
description: The world's first hanging obelisk, relocated from Tanis to the museum entrance. Visitors can stand beneath it and look up to see the king's cartouches carved on the hidden base of the monument.

name: Colossal Statue of Ramesses II
description: An 11 m, 83-ton red granite colossus of Ramesses II that greets visitors in the Grand Hall. Rediscovered at Memphis in 1820, it is one of the largest royal statues surviving from ancient Egypt.

name: Column of King Merenptah
description: A monumental granite column inscribed with royal names and titles of Merenptah, son and successor of Ramesses II, standing in the Grand Hall beside the colossus.

name: Ptolemaic Royal Statue (pair) in the Grand Hall
description: Two large Ptolemaic statues in the atrium show how Greek-era rulers presented themselves in traditional Egyptian royal style as pharaohs.

name: Royal Statue Group - Royal Image Landing
description: Lowest landing of the staircase: royal statuary that shows how kings used monumental portraits to express power, divinity and the ideal of kingship.

name: Colossal Statue of Senwosret I
description: A colossal granite statue of Senwosret I from the temple of Karnak, a masterpiece of Middle Kingdom royal sculpture with a calm idealised face.

name: Shrine Elements Dedicated to the Gods
description: Carved doorways, naoi and temple elements dedicated by kings to the gods, displayed as 'Divine Houses' along the staircase to show how temples housed the divine.

name: Statue of a God Presented by a King
description: Divine and royal statues side by side in the 'Gods & Kings' section illustrate the relationship between the pharaoh and the deities who legitimised his rule.

name: King List of the Subsidiary Staircase
description: A remarkable king list with a large informational panel on the side staircase, naming rulers in order and showing how Egyptians recorded their own history.

name: Statue of Senwosret I (Side Staircase)
description: Statues of Senwosret I stand beside the king list on the side staircase, representing the founder-like image of a powerful Middle Kingdom ruler.

name: Head of Akhenaten
description: A stone head of Akhenaten placed across the stairs from the other kings, suggesting a pharaoh apart. Its elongated features show the radical Amarna art style of the sun-worshipping king.

name: Restoration Stela of Tutankhamun
description: The Restoration Stela, flanked by two statues of the king, records how Tutankhamun restored the traditional gods and temples after the Amarna upheaval and links the staircase to the Tutankhamun galleries.

name: Funerary Monument - Journey to Eternity
description: Monuments in the 'Journey to Eternity' section illustrate beliefs about death, burial and rebirth carved onto stone coffins, stelae and tomb architecture.

name: Pyramid Panorama Window
description: A floor-to-ceiling window at the top of the Grand Staircase frames a panoramic view of the Giza pyramids, linking the museum to the monuments of Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure.

name: Solar Boat of Khufu
description: A 43 m cedar boat found in a pit beside the Great Pyramid, believed to carry King Khufu with the sun god Ra in the afterlife. It is the oldest and largest wooden boat discovered in Egypt.

name: Second Solar Boat of Khufu (under conservation)
description: The second boat from the sealed pits at Giza is still being studied and restored, and visitors can watch conservators at work.

name: Khufu Boat Rope and Reed Mat Fragments
description: Ropes, mats and tools found with the boats show how ancient shipwrights assembled the vessel without nails.

name: Predynastic Painted Pottery Vessel
description: Buff clay vessels painted with boats, animals and spirals show the settled farming communities of the Nile Valley before the first pharaohs.

name: Flint Knife with Ripple Flaking
description: A beautifully flaked flint blade shows the craft of Predynastic stone workers and the early development of prestige weapons.

name: Palette for Grinding Eye Paint
description: Slate palettes used to grind malachite for eye makeup became carved ceremonial objects as society grew more hierarchical.

name: Early Dynastic Stone Vessel
description: Hard stone vessels carved by Early Dynastic craftsmen reflect royal workshops and elite funerary gifts.

name: Animal Figurine of Predynastic Egypt
description: Small animal figures made of clay and ivory hint at early beliefs and the importance of cattle, hippopotami and birds in Nile life.

name: Old Kingdom Agricultural Scene Relief
description: Painted limestone relief from a tomb chapel shows farming, herding and fishing, everyday work that fed the pyramid-building state.

name: Statue of the Scribe Mitri
description: A painted wooden statue of the official Mitri, shown as a scribe with a lifelike face, representing the literate administrators who ran Old Kingdom Egypt.

name: Servant Statuettes Grinding Grain and Brewing Beer
description: Tiny wooden servants grinding grain, baking bread and brewing beer were placed in tombs to supply the owner with food for eternity.

name: Burial Equipment of Queen Hetepheres I
description: Almost complete burial equipment of Queen Hetepheres, mother of Khufu, including gilded furniture and a canopy, found near the Great Pyramid and shown with objects never exhibited before.

name: Silver Bracelets of Queen Hetepheres
description: Delicate silver bracelets inlaid with colourful stones belonged to the mother of Khufu, showing early royal jewelry design.

name: Pyramid Builders' Royal Statue Head
description: A carved royal head from the age of the Giza pyramids with the idealised features that expressed the divine kingship of the Old Kingdom.

name: Early Dynastic King's Name Inscription (Serekh)
description: Carved royal names enclosed in the serekh frame show the first appearance of hieroglyphic writing in the service of kingship and state formation.

name: Pyramid Complex Relief Fragment
description: Relief fragments from a royal funerary temple depict the king with the gods and give clues to pyramid-complex ritual and decoration.

name: Statue of King Pepi I (Copper Statue Type)
description: Metal royal sculpture of the late Old Kingdom demonstrates early copper-working techniques and the continuing importance of royal portraiture.

name: Old Kingdom False Door Stela
description: A carved false door allowed the spirit of the tomb owner to receive offerings, expressing early beliefs about the afterlife and the cult of the dead.

name: Pyramid Texts Inscription Fragment
description: Spells carved in royal pyramids, the oldest religious texts in the world, guided the dead king to the sky and the company of the gods.

name: Early Funerary Offering Table
description: Offering tables carved with bread, beer and meat were set in front of tombs to feed the soul of the deceased for eternity.

name: Predynastic Burial in Contracted Position
description: A reconstruction of an early grave shows the body naturally preserved in the desert sand, the observation that inspired later mummification.

name: Early Amulets of Animal Gods
description: Small amulets shaped like falcons, cows and jackals reflect the earliest animal-form deities and the protection they offered the living and the dead.

name: Painted Wooden Soldiers of Mesehti (Egyptian Spearmen)
description: Forty painted wooden Egyptian spearmen from the tomb of the nomarch Mesehti at Asyut, each face unique and each holding a lance and shield, a rare view of the army of the Middle Kingdom.

name: Painted Wooden Nubian Archers of Mesehti
description: Forty painted Nubian archers from the same tomb accompany the Egyptian spearmen, showing foreign soldiers serving in the Egyptian army.

name: Model of Funerary Boat of Ukhhotep
description: A painted wooden model of a funerary boat discovered at Meir, showing the funeral journey of the nomarch Ukhhotep across the Nile.

name: Model Workshop of Carpenters and Weavers
description: Tomb models of busy workshops with carpenters, weavers and brewers give a miniature view of craft production in a Middle Kingdom estate.

name: Model Granary with Scribes Counting Grain
description: A model granary with scribes recording the harvest shows the bureaucracy and taxation system of the Middle Kingdom.

name: Middle Kingdom Cattle Counting Model
description: A model of the owner inspecting his cattle illustrates wealth measured in livestock and the role of animals in provincial life.

name: Hyksos Scarab Seal Collection
description: Scarab seals of Hyksos rulers from the Delta tell the story of foreign kings who governed part of Egypt during the Second Intermediate Period.

name: Portrait of Senusret III
description: Psychologically realistic portraits of Senusret III show a tired, thoughtful king, a dramatic break from the idealised royal faces of earlier periods.

name: Colossal Granite Statue of Senwosret I from Karnak (GEM 1706)
description: A colossal granite statue of Senwosret I from the temple of Karnak stands in the Middle Kingdom galleries, one of the largest royal sculptures of the era.

name: Middle Kingdom Royal Sphinx
description: A royal sphinx combining a lion's body with the king's head symbolises royal power guarding the sacred space of the temple.

name: Royal Jewelry of a Middle Kingdom Princess
description: Crowns, pectorals and bracelets of gold inlaid with carnelian and turquoise reveal the high point of Egyptian jewelry production under the Middle Kingdom.

name: Pyramid Capstone of a Middle Kingdom King
description: A carved pyramidion shows that Middle Kingdom kings returned to pyramid building, with decoration of the sun's journey.

name: Foundation Deposit of a Royal Temple
description: Models, tools and offerings buried under temple walls consecrated new royal buildings.

name: Royal Stela Recording Nubian Campaigns
description: A border stela proclaiming the limits of Egyptian territory in Nubia shows the king as a military leader.

name: Middle Kingdom Coffin with Coffin Texts
description: A rectangular wooden coffin painted with eyes and covered in hieroglyphic spells known as Coffin Texts to guide the owner through the underworld.

name: Mask and Canopic Box of a Middle Kingdom Official
description: A painted funerary mask and canopic box guarded the face and organs of a provincial official on his journey to eternity.

name: Osiris Statuette of the Middle Kingdom
description: The god Osiris, ruler of the dead, appears in mummiform shape in growing popular devotion during the Middle Kingdom.

name: Poetry and Literature on Papyrus (Middle Kingdom)
description: Papyrus fragments of stories and poetry remind visitors that the Middle Kingdom was the classical age of Egyptian literature.

name: Hathor Cow Amulet and Jewelry Set
description: Jewelry with a Hathor cow motif combined fashion with divine protection, and was worn by women of the court.

name: Model Boats Sailing to Abydos
description: A pair of model boats represents the pilgrimage to Abydos, the cult centre of Osiris, that every Egyptian hoped to make in life or death.

name: Statue of the Scribe Paramessu (Ramesses I as Vizier)
description: A scribe statue of Paramessu, the vizier who later became King Ramesses I, shows the route from official to founder of the Ramesside dynasty.

name: Statuette of a Falcon
description: A gilt bronze votive statuette of a hawk discovered in 1893, dedicated to the falcon god Horus.

name: New Kingdom Domestic Furniture - Stool and Headrest
description: Folding stools, chairs and carved headrests give a close look at the furnishings in the homes of New Kingdom elites.

name: Cosmetic Box and Mirror of a Noblewoman
description: A cosmetic box with kohl tubes, combs and a polished bronze mirror shows beauty routines in ancient Egypt.

name: Workers' Village Ostraca and Tools
description: Pottery and limestone fragments with sketches and notes from the workers who built royal tombs reveal their daily life, strikes and humour.

name: Amarna Period Relief of a Royal Family
description: A relief showing a royal family beneath the rays of the sun disc Aten shows the intimate, naturalistic style of the Amarna Period.

name: Senet Game Board of the New Kingdom
description: A senet board game, played by all classes and believed to symbolise the journey to the afterlife, can be compared with the one from Tutankhamun's tomb.

name: Statue of Queen Hatshepsut
description: A statue of Queen Hatshepsut, the woman who ruled as pharaoh, shows her in royal regalia and expresses her claim to kingship.

name: Thutmose III as King and Scribe
description: A statue of the warrior-king Thutmose III shown with scribal equipment, combining the image of conqueror and learned ruler.

name: Ramesses II Smiting Enemies Relief
description: A relief of the king striking down foreign enemies is the classic image of pharaonic power and propaganda after the battle of Kadesh.

name: Royal Chariot Fittings of Thutmose IV
description: Chariot fittings show the new technology introduced by the Hyksos that made the New Kingdom army so powerful.

name: Pharaoh's Khepresh War Crown and Regalia
description: The blue Khepresh crown and royal sceptres illustrate how New Kingdom pharaohs displayed royal and military authority.

name: Diplomatic Amarna Letters Tablet
description: Cuneiform clay tablets of international correspondence show the New Kingdom as a diplomatic great power.

name: Winged Scarab Pectoral
description: A gold pectoral with a winged scarab inlaid with lapis and carnelian, symbol of the rising sun and rebirth, worn or buried to protect the body.

name: Book of the Dead Papyrus
description: A painted papyrus with spells of the Book of the Dead and the weighing of the heart ceremony before Osiris.

name: Set of Shabti Figures
description: Small servant figures called shabtis were meant to work for the deceased in the field of reeds.

name: Anthropoid Coffin of a Priest of Amun
description: A human-shaped coffin painted with protective gods and a golden face for a priest of Amun at Thebes.

name: Canopic Jars with Four Sons of Horus
description: Four jars with the heads of Imseti, Hapy, Duamutef and Qebehsenuef guarded the mummified liver, lungs, stomach and intestines.

name: Statue of the God Amun
description: A statue of Amun, king of the gods and patron of Thebes, associated with state religion and imperial power.

name: Mummy of a New Kingdom Official
description: A mummy and its wrappings show how embalmers preserved the body and how modern CT scanning reveals what lies under the linen.

name: Heart Scarab of a Noble
description: A heart scarab placed on the mummy's chest carried a spell to stop the heart from testifying against its owner in the judgement.

name: Golden Burial Mask of Tutankhamun
material: Solid gold with semi-precious stones and glass
description: The iconic gold funerary mask of the boy king, lit as the centrepiece of the Tutankhamun galleries, weighing about 11 kg and inlaid with lapis lazuli, quartz and obsidian.

name: Solid Gold Inner Coffin of Tutankhamun
description: The innermost of three nested coffins, made of solid gold in the form of the god Osiris, held the mummy of the king.

name: Middle Coffin of Tutankhamun
description: The middle coffin, covered with gold leaf and inlaid with glass, is part of a stepwise programme of protection and renewal.

name: Outer Gilded Coffin of Tutankhamun
description: The outer coffin, restored before going on view, shows the king as Osiris with feather patterns and protective winged goddesses.

name: Quartzite Sarcophagus of Tutankhamun
description: The stone sarcophagus with goddesses protecting the corners enclosed the three coffins in the burial chamber.

name: Gilded Shrines of Tutankhamun (Nested Shrines)
description: A set of gilded wooden shrines nested one inside the other surrounded the sarcophagus, covered in funerary texts and divine figures.

name: Canopic Shrine with Four Guardian Goddesses
description: A gilded shrine guarded by four goddesses (Isis, Nephthys, Neith and Selket) protects the calcite canopic chest that held the king's organs.

name: Miniature Gold Canopic Coffins
description: Four miniature coffins of gold inside the alabaster canopic chest contained the king's embalmed internal organs, among the most delicate objects in the collection.

name: Golden Throne of Tutankhamun
description: The gilded wooden throne, with a backrest showing Queen Ankhesenamun anointing the king, is one of the finest examples of royal furniture ever found.

name: Six Chariots of Tutankhamun
description: Six complete but dismantled chariots with different wheels and lashings, including golden ceremonial vehicles, show the king's role as warrior and hunter.

name: Shields and Ceremonial Daggers of Tutankhamun
description: Court and combat gear including shields and two daggers, one with an iron blade made from meteoritic metal.

name: Painted Chest with War and Hunting Scenes
description: A wooden chest painted with the king triumphing over Nubians and Asiatics and hunting wild animals, a rare example of royal painting.

name: Ceremonial Bows and Arrows of Tutankhamun
description: Bows decorated with gold and bark show the king's training in archery.

name: Golden Fan and Ostrich Feather Fan
description: A golden fan with ostrich feather remains records a hunt in the desert and the king's royal image.

name: Tutankhamun's Senet and Game Boxes
description: Game boxes for senet and related board games used for leisure and symbolic of the soul's journey.

name: Child's Chair and Personal Furniture of the King
description: Chairs, stools and headrests, some from the king's childhood, provide a human view of the pharaoh's daily life.

name: Linen Clothing and Gold Sandals of Tutankhamun
description: Tunics, gloves and gold sandals show what the king wore, and how fine linen and gold were combined in royal dress.

name: Silver Trumpet of Tutankhamun
description: One of two trumpets found in the tomb, played in religious and military ceremony.

name: Pectoral with Winged Scarab of Tutankhamun
description: A pectoral with a scarab bearing the sun disc in lapis and carnelian, one of many pieces of royal jewelry from the king's treasury.

name: Anubis Shrine with Jackal on Sled
description: A black jackal figure on a gilded shrine guarded the treasury and the entrance to the realm of the dead.

name: Guardian Statues of the King (Sentinels)
description: Two life-size black and gold statues stood on either side of the burial chamber entrance as protectors of the king.

name: Howard Carter's Excavation Archive and Photographs
description: Carter's notes, drawings and photographs tell the story of the discovery of KV62 in 1922 and the ten years it took to clear the tomb.

name: Tomb Entrance Seals and Tomb Reconstruction
description: Reconstructions of the antechamber, annex, burial chamber and treasury of KV62 show how the tomb looked when Howard Carter first entered.

name: Family Tree and Identity of Tutankhamun
description: A section on his name, parents and possible family tree, including Akhenaten, Nefertiti and Ankhesenamun.

name: Golden Bed in the Form of Cow Goddess
description: A ceremonial bed in the shape of a cow, possibly linked with Hathor or Mehetweret, used in rebirth ritual.

name: Ushabti Figures of Tutankhamun
description: More than four hundred servant figures to do the king's work in the afterlife.

name: Calcite Wishing Cup of Tutankhamun
description: A lotus-shaped alabaster cup with inscriptions wishing the king millions of years of life.

name: Golden Shrine of Hathor Goddess Statue
description: A gilded statue of a deity protecting the king on his journey into the afterlife.

name: Tutankhamun's Alabaster Lamps and Vessels
description: Translucent calcite vessels and lamps carved with floral decoration were used to light the tomb and hold ritual oils.

name: Tutankhamun Statue as Harpooner on a Papyrus Raft
description: The king stands on a papyrus raft in a harpooner pose, symbolically defeating chaos.

name: Late Period Bronze Statuette of a Cat Goddess
description: Votive bronzes of cats dedicated to Bastet were made in thousands during the Late Period by pilgrims.

name: Persian-Period Seal and Administrative Documents
description: Seals and demotic documents show how Egyptians lived under Persian rule.

name: Kushite King Portrait Head (25th Dynasty)
description: A portrait of a Nubian pharaoh wearing the double uraeus, the symbol of the Kushite kings of Egypt and Nubia.

name: Late Period Household Items and Jewelry
description: Household objects and bead jewelry from a Late Period town give insight into everyday life.

name: Egyptian Priests' Statues in Realistic Style
description: Realistic statues of priests with shaved heads and lifelike faces show a revival of older art.

name: Dendera Treasure Hoard - Gold and Silver Falcon
description: A hollow falcon made of gold and silver from the Dendera treasure hoards, hidden in the temple perhaps by priests; it may once have contained a mummified bird.

name: Dendera Treasure Hoard - Outer Falcon Coffin
description: The 60 cm tall outer coffin of a falcon from the Dendera treasure shows how sacred animals were buried.

name: Dendera Treasure Hoard - Sacred Ritual Vessels
description: Ritual vessels from the temple hoard of Dendera illustrate the wealth of the temple and its priests.

name: Statue of a Ptolemaic King in Egyptian Dress
description: A Greek pharaoh shown as a traditional Egyptian king with nemes headcloth.

name: Kushite Royal Objects of the 25th Dynasty
description: Royal objects from the Nubian pharaohs who ruled Egypt and reunited the Nile Valley.

name: Rosetta-Style Decree Stela (Ptolemaic)
description: A priestly decree in hieroglyphic, demotic and Greek, the multilingual administration of Greek-ruled Egypt.

name: Adult Crocodile Mummy
description: A full-size adult crocodile mummy in contrast to most crocodile mummies that are of baby animals, dedicated to the crocodile god Sobek.

name: Fayum Mummy Portrait
description: A realistic painted portrait attached to a mummy from the Roman Period, blending Greek painting with Egyptian burial customs.

name: Statue of the Goddess Isis in Greco-Roman Style
description: Isis, worshipped across the Roman Empire, appears in a statue that merges Egyptian and Greek forms.

name: Animal Mummies: Ibis, Cat and Falcon
description: Mummified ibis, cats and falcons were offerings to gods such as Thoth, Bastet and Horus.

name: Roman-Period Painted Shroud
description: A painted burial shroud with the deceased beside Osiris and Anubis, showing continuing funerary belief.

name: Roman Mummy with Gilded Mask
description: A mummy decorated with a gilded cartonnage mask and elaborate wrapping, typical of Roman Egypt.

name: Serapis Statue
description: The Greco-Egyptian god Serapis, created under the Ptolemies to unite two religions.

name: Coptic-Roman Funerary Stela
description: A funerary stela shows the late phase of ancient Egyptian belief as new religions arrived.
